description: Comprehensive Syllogism question bank derived from supplied Mental Ability notes. Covers fundamentals, quantifiers, Venn diagrams, conclusion testing, possibility conclusions, 'only/few' wording, common errors, and solved/practice patterns. Verify against official exam convention before formal use.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a syllogism?

options.A: A mathematical equation solved by elimination
options.B: A logical argument in which conclusions are tested using given statements or premises
options.C: A diagram showing only numerical data
options.D: A method of guessing answers from real-world knowledge

questions.explanation: A syllogism is a form of deductive reasoning in which conclusions are tested using given statements or premises.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a statement in a syllogism?

options.A: A conclusion drawn from the premises
options.B: A premise accepted as true for the purpose of the question
options.C: A real-world fact that must be verified
options.D: An optional hint given in the question

questions.explanation: A statement is a premise accepted as true for the purpose of the question; it may describe a relationship between two or more groups.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a conclusion in a syllogism?

options.A: A premise given at the start of the question
options.B: A proposition that must logically follow from the given statements
options.C: An assumption based on general knowledge
options.D: A statement that is always factually true

questions.explanation: A conclusion is a proposition that must logically follow from the given statements.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a premise?

options.A: A given statement used as the basis for drawing a conclusion
options.B: The final answer selected from the options
options.C: A diagram drawn after testing conclusions
options.D: A conclusion that is possibly true

questions.explanation: A premise is a given statement used as the basis for drawing a conclusion.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the main rule for solving syllogisms?

options.A: Verify each statement against real-world facts before accepting it
options.B: Accept the statements as true even if they appear contrary to real-world facts, and select only conclusions that necessarily follow
options.C: Reject any statement that seems unusual in real life
options.D: Choose the conclusion that seems most likely in practice

questions.explanation: Accept the statements as true, even if they appear contrary to real-world facts, and select only conclusions that necessarily follow from them.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Should outside knowledge be used in a syllogism?

options.A: Yes, to verify whether the statements are realistic
options.B: Yes, only when the statements are about science
options.C: No, use only the logical information contained in the given statements
options.D: Yes, whenever the conclusion seems factually correct

questions.explanation: No. Use only the logical information contained in the given statements. Do not add assumptions based on common knowledge.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is meant by 'definitely follows' in a syllogism?

options.A: The conclusion is true in at least one arrangement of the premises
options.B: The conclusion is true in every possible arrangement that satisfies all the given statements
options.C: The conclusion matches real-world facts
options.D: The conclusion is stated directly in one of the premises

questions.explanation: A conclusion definitely follows when it is true in every possible arrangement that satisfies all the given statements.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is meant by 'may be true' in a syllogism?

options.A: The conclusion is true in every arrangement of the premises
options.B: The conclusion is false in every arrangement of the premises
options.C: At least one arrangement satisfies the conclusion, but another arrangement may make it false
options.D: The conclusion is directly given as a premise

questions.explanation: A conclusion may be true when at least one arrangement satisfies it, but another arrangement may make it false. Possibility is not the same as certainty.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a statement and a conclusion?

options.A: A statement is tested; a conclusion is supplied as a premise
options.B: A statement is supplied as a premise; a conclusion is tested to determine whether it is necessarily supported by the premises
options.C: Both are supplied as premises and both are tested
options.D: A statement is always false; a conclusion is always true

questions.explanation: A statement is supplied as a premise; a conclusion is tested to determine whether it is necessarily supported by the premises.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the objective of a Venn diagram in syllogism?

options.A: To calculate numerical values of the sets
options.B: To visually represent set relationships stated in the premises and help test whether a proposed conclusion must be true
options.C: To replace the statements with real-world facts
options.D: To show only the conclusion without the premises

questions.explanation: A Venn diagram visually represents the set relationships stated in the premises and helps test whether a proposed conclusion must be true.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'All A are B' mean?

options.A: Every member of set A is also a member of set B
options.B: Every member of set B is also a member of set A
options.C: At least one member is common to A and B
options.D: No member of A belongs to B

questions.explanation: Every member of set A is also a member of set B. Set A is completely contained within set B; B may contain members that are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'No A is B' mean?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: At least one A is B
options.C: Sets A and B have no common members; they are completely separate or disjoint
options.D: Some A are not B

questions.explanation: Sets A and B have no common members; they are completely separate or disjoint.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Some A are B' mean?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: At least one member belongs to both A and B, establishing an intersection
options.C: No A is B
options.D: At least one member of A lies outside B

questions.explanation: At least one member belongs to both A and B. The statement establishes an intersection between the two sets.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Some A are not B' mean?

options.A: At least one member of A lies outside set B
options.B: No member of A lies outside B
options.C: All A are B
options.D: Some B are not A

questions.explanation: At least one member of A lies outside set B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does 'All A are B' mean 'All B are A'?

options.A: Yes, the relationship is always reversible
options.B: No, because A is inside B but B may contain other members
options.C: Yes, only when A and B are equal in size
options.D: No, because 'All A are B' means no A is B

questions.explanation: No. 'All A are B' places A inside B, but B may contain other members. The reverse statement is not guaranteed.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does 'No A is B' imply 'No B is A'?

options.A: No, the relationship is one-way only
options.B: Yes, the relationship is symmetric: if A and B have no common members, neither set has a member in the other
options.C: Yes, but only if A exists
options.D: No, because B may contain A

questions.explanation: Yes. The relationship is symmetric: if A and B have no common members, neither set has a member in the other.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does 'Some A are B' imply 'Some B are A'?

options.A: No, the common member is not shared both ways
options.B: Yes, the same common member belongs to both A and B
options.C: Yes, but only if all A are B
options.D: No, unless A and B are identical sets

questions.explanation: Yes. The same common member belongs to both A and B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does 'Some A are not B' imply 'Some B are not A'?

options.A: Yes, the relationship is always symmetric
options.B: No, the member of A outside B says nothing about whether B has a member outside A
options.C: Yes, because some A are B
options.D: No, because 'Some A are not B' means no A is B

questions.explanation: No. The member of A outside B says nothing about whether B has a member outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'All A are B' and 'Some A are B'?

options.A: There is no difference; both mean at least one A is B
options.B: 'All A are B' includes every member of A within B; 'Some A are B' asserts only at least one common member
options.C: 'Some A are B' includes every member of A within B; 'All A are B' asserts only one common member
options.D: 'All A are B' means no A is B

questions.explanation: 'All A are B' includes every member of A within B; 'Some A are B' asserts only at least one common member.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'No A is B' and 'Some A are not B'?

options.A: There is no difference; both mean no A is B
options.B: 'No A is B' says every A is outside B; 'Some A are not B' says only at least one A is outside B
options.C: 'Some A are not B' says every A is outside B; 'No A is B' says only one A is outside B
options.D: 'No A is B' means at least one A is B

questions.explanation: 'No A is B' says every A is outside B; 'Some A are not B' says only at least one A is outside B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'All' mean in syllogism?

options.A: A particular affirmative statement: at least one member belongs
options.B: A universal affirmative statement: every member of the subject class belongs to the predicate class
options.C: A universal negative statement: no member belongs
options.D: A particular negative statement: at least one member does not belong

questions.explanation: It is a universal affirmative statement: every member of the subject class belongs to the predicate class.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'No' mean in syllogism?

options.A: A universal affirmative statement
options.B: A particular affirmative statement
options.C: A universal negative statement: no member of the subject class belongs to the predicate class
options.D: A particular negative statement

questions.explanation: It is a universal negative statement: no member of the subject class belongs to the predicate class.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Some' mean in syllogism?

options.A: It means all members without exception
options.B: It means at least one; it does not mean some but not all unless the wording explicitly says so
options.C: It means no member at all
options.D: It means exactly half of the members

questions.explanation: It means at least one. It does not mean some but not all unless the wording explicitly says some but not all.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Some ... are not' mean?

options.A: At least one member of the first group is outside the second group
options.B: All members of the first group are outside the second group
options.C: No member of the first group is outside the second group
options.D: All members of the second group are outside the first group

questions.explanation: At least one member of the first group is outside the second group.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Only A are B' mean?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: All B are A
options.C: Some A are B
options.D: No B is A

questions.explanation: 'Only A are B' means all B are A. The word 'only' reverses the apparent direction: A is the necessary category for B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'Only a few A are B' commonly mean in aptitude questions?

options.A: All A are B
options.B: No A is B
options.C: Some A are B and some A are not B
options.D: All B are A

questions.explanation: It means some A are B and some A are not B. The exact convention used by the exam should be followed if specified.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A few A are B' mean?

options.A: Some A are B; it does not by itself establish that some A are not B
options.B: Some A are B and some A are not B always
options.C: All A are B
options.D: No A is B

questions.explanation: 'A few A are B' means some A are B; it does not by itself establish that some A are not B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is not B' mean in a categorical statement?

options.A: For an individual, A does not belong to category B; it should not be automatically generalised to an entire group unless the statement does so
options.B: No member of the group A belongs to B
options.C: All members of A belong to B
options.D: Some members of B belong to A

questions.explanation: For an individual, it states that the person or object A does not belong to category B. Do not automatically generalise it to an entire group unless the statement does so.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'At least some A are B' mean?

options.A: No A is B
options.B: Some A are B, so at least one member is common to the two sets
options.C: All A are B
options.D: Some A are not B

questions.explanation: It means some A are B, so at least one member is common to the two sets.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'At most some' mean in syllogism?

options.A: It is a standard universal quantifier equivalent to 'All'
options.B: It is a standard particular quantifier equivalent to 'Some'
options.C: It is not a standard basic categorical quantifier; interpret it from the exact wording and avoid treating it as a standard universal or particular proposition
options.D: It means 'No'

questions.explanation: This is not a standard basic categorical quantifier. Interpret it from the exact wording and avoid treating it as a standard universal or particular proposition.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a Venn diagram?

options.A: A table of numerical values
options.B: A diagram that uses circles or other closed shapes to represent sets and their intersections, inclusions, or separation
options.C: A list of conclusions ranked by probability
options.D: A method of solving equations graphically

questions.explanation: A Venn diagram uses circles or other closed shapes to represent sets and their intersections, inclusions, or separation.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is 'All A are B' represented in a Venn diagram?

options.A: Draw circle A completely inside circle B
options.B: Draw circles A and B separately without overlap
options.C: Draw overlapping circles with an X in the common region
options.D: Place an X in the part of A outside B

questions.explanation: Draw circle A completely inside circle B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is 'No A is B' represented in a Venn diagram?

options.A: Draw circle A inside circle B
options.B: Draw overlapping circles with an X in the common region
options.C: Draw circles A and B separately, without overlap
options.D: Place an X in the part of A outside B

questions.explanation: Draw circles A and B separately, without overlap.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is 'Some A are B' represented in a Venn diagram?

options.A: Draw circle A inside circle B
options.B: Draw overlapping circles A and B and place an X in the common region to show at least one member exists there
options.C: Draw circles A and B separately
options.D: Place an X in the part of A outside B

questions.explanation: Draw overlapping circles A and B and place an X in the common region to show at least one member exists there.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is 'Some A are not B' represented in a Venn diagram?

options.A: Place an X in the part of circle A that lies outside circle B
options.B: Draw circle A inside circle B
options.C: Draw circles A and B separately
options.D: Place an X in the common region of A and B

questions.explanation: Place an X in the part of circle A that lies outside circle B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does an X represent in a syllogism Venn diagram?

options.A: An empty region with no members
options.B: The existence of at least one member in the region where it is placed
options.C: A region that must be ignored
options.D: The conclusion to be tested

questions.explanation: An X represents the existence of at least one member in the region where it is placed.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does shading represent in a Venn diagram?

options.A: The existence of at least one member
options.B: An empty region, meaning that no member can exist in that region
options.C: A region that may or may not have members
options.D: The conclusion that definitely follows

questions.explanation: Shading represents an empty region, meaning that no member can exist in that region.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why should an X sometimes be placed on a boundary line in a syllogism Venn diagram?

options.A: To show that the region is empty
options.B: When the premises establish that an object exists in one of two possible regions but do not determine which one, the X is placed on the dividing boundary to show the uncertainty
options.C: To indicate that the conclusion is false
options.D: To mark the largest set in the diagram

questions.explanation: When the premises establish that an object exists in one of two possible regions but do not determine which one, the X is placed on the dividing boundary to show the uncertainty.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is 'All A are B' different from 'Some A are B' in a Venn diagram?

options.A: There is no difference in representation
options.B: For 'All A are B', A is contained in B but no existence of A is automatically marked in modern Boolean interpretation; for 'Some A are B', an X must be placed in the overlap
options.C: For 'Some A are B', A is contained in B; for 'All A are B', an X is placed in the overlap
options.D: Both require circles drawn separately without overlap

questions.explanation: For 'All A are B', A is contained in B but no existence of A is automatically marked in modern Boolean interpretation. For 'Some A are B', an X must be placed in the overlap.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How can a Venn diagram test a conclusion?

options.A: Draw the conclusion first and then fit the premises into it
options.B: Draw all premise relationships first; then check whether the conclusion is true in every arrangement allowed by the diagram; if it is not guaranteed, it does not definitely follow
options.C: Draw only the conclusion and ignore the premises
options.D: Use real-world knowledge instead of the diagram

questions.explanation: Draw all premise relationships first. Then check whether the conclusion is true in every arrangement allowed by the diagram. If it is not guaranteed, it does not definitely follow.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Should a conclusion be used while drawing the Venn diagram?

options.A: Yes, the conclusion must be drawn first to guide the diagram
options.B: No, draw the diagram only from the premises, then test each conclusion independently
options.C: Yes, but only when the conclusion is a possibility
options.D: Yes, the conclusion replaces one of the premises in the diagram

questions.explanation: No. Draw the diagram only from the premises, then test each conclusion independently.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the main Venn-diagram mistake in syllogism?

options.A: Drawing circles for every set mentioned
options.B: Treating a possible arrangement as a compulsory one; a conclusion follows only if every arrangement satisfying the premises makes it true
options.C: Placing an X to mark existence
options.D: Using shading to mark empty regions

questions.explanation: Treating a possible arrangement as a compulsory one. A conclusion follows only if every arrangement satisfying the premises makes it true.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B, what definitely follows about A?

options.A: Every A is B; therefore 'Some A are B' does not necessarily follow under modern Boolean logic unless the existence of A is separately established
options.B: Every A is B and some A are B necessarily follows
options.C: All B are A necessarily follows
options.D: No A is B necessarily follows

questions.explanation: Every A is B. Therefore, 'Some A are B' does not necessarily follow under modern Boolean logic unless the existence of A is separately established.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B, does 'All B are A' follow?

options.A: Yes, the relationship is symmetric
options.B: No, B may contain members that are not A
options.C: Yes, but only if A exists
options.D: No, because all A are B means no A is B

questions.explanation: No. B may contain members that are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B, does 'Some B are A' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: Not necessarily under modern Boolean logic, because the premises do not guarantee that any A exists
options.C: Yes, because every A is B
options.D: No, because all B are not A

questions.explanation: Not necessarily under modern Boolean logic, because the premises do not guarantee that any A exists.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If no A is B, what definitely follows?

options.A: No B is A; the two sets are disjoint
options.B: Some A are not B necessarily
options.C: All A are B
options.D: Some B are not A necessarily

questions.explanation: No B is A. The two sets are disjoint.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If no A is B, does 'Some A are not B' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: Not necessarily under modern Boolean logic, because the premises do not guarantee that A exists
options.C: Yes, because no A is B means every A is outside B
options.D: No, because some A are B

questions.explanation: Not necessarily under modern Boolean logic, because the premises do not guarantee that A exists.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B, what definitely follows?

options.A: 'Some B are A' also follows, because at least one member is common to both sets
options.B: All A are B follows
options.C: No A is B follows
options.D: Some A are not B follows

questions.explanation: 'Some B are A' also follows, because at least one member is common to both sets.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B, does 'All A are B' follow?

options.A: Yes, one common member establishes every A belongs to B
options.B: No, one common member does not establish that every A belongs to B
options.C: Yes, but only if A exists
options.D: No, because some A are B means no A is B

questions.explanation: No. One common member does not establish that every A belongs to B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are not B, what definitely follows?

options.A: At least one A is outside B; it does not establish any relationship between all members of A and B
options.B: No A is B
options.C: All A are B
options.D: Some B are not A

questions.explanation: At least one A is outside B. It does not establish any relationship between all members of A and B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and all B are C, what follows?

options.A: All A are C, because A is contained in B and B is contained in C
options.B: All C are A
options.C: No A is C
options.D: Some A are not C

questions.explanation: All A are C, because A is contained in B and B is contained in C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and no B is C, what follows?

options.A: All A are C
options.B: No A is C, because every A is inside B and B has no overlap with C
options.C: Some A are C
options.D: No B is A

questions.explanation: No A is C, because every A is inside B and B has no overlap with C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B and all B are C, what follows?

options.A: All A are C
options.B: Some A are C, because the member that is both A and B must also be C
options.C: No A is C
options.D: Some A are not C

questions.explanation: Some A are C. The member that is both A and B must also be C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B and no B is C, what follows?

options.A: Some A are not C, because the A that belongs to B cannot belong to C
options.B: All A are C
options.C: No A is C
options.D: Some A are C

questions.explanation: Some A are not C, because the A that belongs to B cannot belong to C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and some B are C, does 'Some A are C' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: No, the B members that are C may lie outside A
options.C: Yes, because all A are B
options.D: No, because all B are C

questions.explanation: No. The B members that are C may lie outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B and some B are C, does 'Some A are C' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: No, the A-B common member and B-C common member may be different members of B
options.C: Yes, because some B are both A and C
options.D: No, because no A is C

questions.explanation: No. The A-B common member and B-C common member may be different members of B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If no A is B and some B are C, what follows about A and C?

options.A: No definite relationship between A and C follows from these premises alone
options.B: No A is C
options.C: Some A are C
options.D: All A are C

questions.explanation: No definite relationship between A and C follows from these premises alone.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and all B are C, what is the relation between A and C?

options.A: All A are C
options.B: All C are A
options.C: No A is C
options.D: Some A are not C

questions.explanation: All A are C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and no B is C, what is the relation between A and C?

options.A: No A is C
options.B: All A are C
options.C: Some A are C
options.D: No C is A but some A are C

questions.explanation: No A is C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If no A is B and all C are A, what is the relation between C and B?

options.A: No C is B, because all C are inside A and A is separate from B
options.B: Some C are B
options.C: All C are B
options.D: No definite relationship follows

questions.explanation: No C is B, because all C are inside A and A is separate from B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B and all B are C, what is the relation between A and C?

options.A: Some A are C
options.B: All A are C
options.C: No A is C
options.D: Some A are not C

questions.explanation: Some A are C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and some A are C, what follows about B and C?

options.A: Some B are C, because every A is B and at least one A is C
options.B: All B are C
options.C: No B is C
options.D: Some B are not C

questions.explanation: Some B are C, because every A is B and at least one A is C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B and all A are C, what follows about B and C?

options.A: Some B are C, because the member that is A and B is also C
options.B: All B are C
options.C: No B is C
options.D: Some B are not C

questions.explanation: Some B are C, because the member that is A and B is also C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and some B are not C, does 'Some A are not C' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: No, the B members outside C may be outside A
options.C: Yes, because all A are B
options.D: No, because all A are C

questions.explanation: No. The B members outside C may be outside A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and no A is C, does 'No B is C' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: No, B may contain members that are also C, provided those members are not A
options.C: Yes, because all A are B
options.D: No, because some B are C

questions.explanation: No. B may contain members that are also C, provided those members are not A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are not B and all A are C, what follows?

options.A: Some C are not B, because the A member outside B is also in C
options.B: All C are not B
options.C: No C is B
options.D: Some C are B

questions.explanation: Some C are not B, because the A member outside B is also in C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If no A is B and no B is C, does 'No A is C' follow?

options.A: Yes, necessarily
options.B: No, A and C may overlap even though both are separate from B
options.C: Yes, because both are separate from B
options.D: No, because some A are C

questions.explanation: No. A and C may overlap even though both are separate from B.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a possibility conclusion in syllogism?

options.A: A conclusion that must be true in every valid arrangement
options.B: A conclusion that asks whether a relationship can be true in at least one arrangement without violating the premises
options.C: A conclusion that is directly stated as a premise
options.D: A conclusion based on real-world facts

questions.explanation: It asks whether a relationship can be true in at least one arrangement without violating the premises.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'definitely follows' and 'is a possibility'?

options.A: There is no difference; both require truth in every arrangement

options.A: 'Some A are B' and 'Some B are A'
options.B: 'All A are B' and 'All B are A'
options.C: 'Some A are not B' and 'Some B are not A'
options.D: 'No A is B' and 'All B are A'

options.B: 'All A are B'

questions.question: If all A are B and some B are C, does 'Some A are C' follow?

options.D: No, because all B are C

questions.question: If some A are B and some B are C, does 'Some A are C' follow?

options.D: No, because no A is C

questions.question: If no A is B and some B are C, what follows about A and C?

options.B: All B are C
options.C: No B is C
options.D: Some B are not C

questions.explanation: Some B are C, because every A is B and at least one A is C.

questions.question: If some A are B and all A are C, what follows about B and C?

options.A: Some B are C, because the member that is A and B is also C

options.C: No B is C
options.D: Some B are not C

questions.explanation: Some B are C, because the member that is A and B is also C.

options.D: No, because all A are C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B and no A is C, does 'No B is C' follow?

options.A: No, B may contain members that are also C, provided those members are not A

options.C: Yes, because all A are B
options.D: No, because some B are C

questions.question: If some A are not B and all A are C, what follows?

questions.explanation: Some C are not B, because the A member outside B is also in C.

options.A: No, A and C may overlap even though both are separate from B

options.D: No, because some A are C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If all A are B, is it possible that some B are A?

options.A: Yes, if A exists; but the premise 'All A are B' alone does not guarantee A's existence under modern Boolean logic
options.B: No, it is impossible
options.C: Yes, and it is guaranteed even if A does not exist
options.D: No, because all B are A is false

questions.explanation: Yes, if A exists. But the premise 'All A are B' alone does not guarantee A's existence under modern Boolean logic.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If some A are B, is it possible that some A are not B?

options.A: Yes, provided A has additional members outside B; the premise does not establish such members but does not prohibit them
options.B: No, some A are B excludes some A are not B
options.C: No, because some A are B means all A are B
options.D: Yes, and it is guaranteed that some A are not B

questions.explanation: Yes, provided A has additional members outside B. The premise 'Some A are B' alone does not establish that such additional members exist, but it does not prohibit them.

options.C: Always as no A is B
options.D: Always as some A are not B

questions.explanation: Usually as all A are B, but read the complete sentence carefully because 'only' may alter the direction depending on its placement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

options.B: A conclusion that is true in every arrangement is treated as possibly true
options.C: A conclusion is tested using real-world knowledge
options.D: A conclusion is tested without drawing a Venn diagram

questions.explanation: A conclusion that is true in one permitted arrangement is not necessarily true in every permitted arrangement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the error of using real-world knowledge?

options.A: Rejecting a conclusion because it seems factually unusual, or accepting it because it is generally true in the real world
options.B: Accepting a conclusion because it follows logically from the premises
options.C: Drawing a Venn diagram from the premises only
options.D: Testing each conclusion independently

questions.explanation: Rejecting a conclusion because it seems factually unusual, or accepting it because it is generally true in the real world. Only the premises control the logical answer.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the error of ignoring the exact quantifier?

options.A: Treating 'all', 'no', 'some', and 'some not' as interchangeable
options.B: Using a Venn diagram to represent the premises
options.C: Placing an X to mark existence
options.D: Shading to mark an empty region

questions.explanation: Treating 'all', 'no', 'some', and 'some not' as interchangeable. Each has a different set meaning.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which of the following is the error of assuming two groups are completely separate without evidence?

options.A: Drawing disjoint circles when the premises do not require separation
options.B: Drawing disjoint circles when the premises require separation
options.C: Drawing overlapping circles when the premises require overlap
options.D: Placing an X on a boundary line

questions.explanation: Drawing disjoint circles when the premises do not require separation. Unspecified relationships should remain open or overlapping as permitted.

options.B: Roses are included in flowers, and plants are included in flowers, therefore roses are plants
